articles.title: NHL Frozen Frenzy 2026 Live Blog: Red Wings, Canadiens, Maple Leafs, Jets And Oilers Headline Nonstop Action
articles.summary: Thirty-two teams collide in a sixteen-game marathon featuring Ovechkin’s farewell in Carolina, Bedard’s anticipated return, and a high-stakes goalie controve...
articles.body:
Thirty-two teams. Sixteen games. All in one night.

Yes, it's NHL Frozen Frenzy — and this year's eight hours or so of madness promises not to disappoint.

Connor Bedard is (reportedly) back with the Chicago Blackhawks. Alex Ovechkin is back — for the last time? — in Carolina. And Mikko Rantanen is back playing against his former team, the Colorado Avalanche.

Will Dylan Larkin get booed by the home fans in Detroit? Will Brady Tkachuk finally score his first goal as a Florida Panther?" Will the Toronto Maple Leafs escape their road trip out west with five out of a possible six points?

More importantly, will we report on all the action? Yes!

Don't forget to follow us @thehockeynews.com and drop a comment or question below in the comments.

"Told it's really quiet. No momentum for a trade right now. That said I get the sense the relationship between larkin and the red wings is at such a place it's just a matter of when not if." — ESPN's Emily Kaplan on Dylan Larkin

1-0 for Devils on a goal from Evan Rodrigues, his first since being traded to New Jersey.

Devils outshooting Red Wings 16-3 after 20 minutes. The score is tied 1-1.

Does Connor Hellebuyck want to play in New Jersey? The Red Wings have given up two goals on four shots.

Jack Hughes scores the overtime winner for New Jersey, ending a wild back-and-forth battle to kick off the Frozen Frenzy.

A bit of good news for the Red Wings, who appear to have signed Alex DeBrincat to a seven-year extension with a $13-million cap hit. The contract, which kicks in next season, makes him the 13th highest-paid NHLer — for now.

Columbus scores and Matthew Knies picks up the assist. The ex-Leaf now has five points in five games.

Brady Tkachuk scores his first goals since joining the Panthers. And, of course, Matthew gets the assist.

Matthew finds Brady alone in the slot for his second.

Four points each for the Tkachuk brothers, who pick up assists on a goal from Carter Verhaeghe.

Kids, don't try this at home: Mathieu Olivier gets a five-minute major and a game misconduct for spearing Uvis (in his) Balinskis. Ouch!

Another assist for Matthew Tkachuk. Watch out, Connor McDavid (10 assists), but Tkachuk is now up to seven assists in seven games.

Big night from the players who were off to cold starts, as Sam Reinhart scores his second of the game.

Is a goalie controversy brewing in Montreal? The Habs appear to be starting Jacob Fowler for the third game in a row.

Buffalo scores on a goal from Owen Zellweger, just first since joining the Sabres I a trade for Bowen Byram.

Tough to watch as linesman falls awkwardly on his ankle . Being helped off the ice.

Lane Hutson gets his first on a point shot on the PP. It was a wrister. But it was a snipe .

Save of the Year alert : UPL stops the Habs on a two-on-none.

Noah Dobson takes a shot off the jaw. With Michael Matheson also out, this is not good for the Habs' defense.

What's going on with Montreal in the third period? Buffalo scores twice in under six minutes to tie things up 3-3, despite being outshot 23-14.

For the second straight game, the Habs are heading to overtime.

Carolina was where Alex Ovechkin was drafted No. 1 overall in 2004 . Twenty-two years later, he's playing in his final regular season game in Raleigh, N.C.

According to @ryanhenkel_ , the Canes recognized Ovechkin during a stoppage in play and he received a standing ovation .

Carolina loses Taylor Hall, who "was ruled out in the second period of Tuesday's game against the Washington Capitals due to an upper-body injury." Hall took a hard hit from Justin Sourdif late in the first period.

Looks like Porter Martone and Matvei Michkov will play together on a line.

Bobby McMann scores his third of the season. With 29 goals split between Toronto and Seattle, he was technically the Kraken's leading goal scorer last season.

Make that seven goals in eight game for breakout candidate Lafreniere.

According to reporter Steve Warne , the Senators have three defensemen tonight who each have played in 10 NHL games or less.

It appears that Zee's Buium has been dropped to the Canucks' third defense pairing alongside Luke Schenn.

Calder Trophy Watch: Chicago's Anton Frondell picks up his fifth assist of the season. He now has five points in seven games.

Sidney Crosby scores his first of the season. Last year, he finished with 29.

From @OHaraSports : "Mackenzie Blackwood is 0-4-1 in six regular season games against the Dallas Stars. He holds a 4.10 goals against average and a .887 save percentage in those appearances. Two of those games came when he was was with the New Jersey Devils, three with the San Jose Sharks, and one with the Colorado Avalanche."

articles.title: Red Bull sends warning to F1 rivals with engine development admission
articles.summary: Red Bull technical director Pierre Wache has rated the team's first in-house Formula 1 power unit project just four or five out of 10
articles.body:
Ask most engineers to grade their own work at four or five out of 10 and you'd brace for bad news. Pierre Wache, Red Bull Racing's technical director, offered that score for the team's first homemade Formula 1 power unit, and it feels like a threat to the rest of the grid. Put simply, Red Bull thinks its in-house engine is somewhere between 40 and 50% of the way to where it can be, and it considers that a good place to start.

Asked by RacingNews365 to rate the project on a scale of one to 10, Wache said: "I'd say a four or a five." When the follow-up asked whether that leaves a lot of room to grow, he warned: "Absolutely, the potential is massive."

Throughout its two decades in Formula 1 from 2005 to 2025, Red Bull relied on external engine manufacturers - Cosworth, Ferrari , Renault, and Honda among them - rather than developing powerplants in-house. Beginning this season, this has changed as the team undertakes its first independent engine program in partnership with Ford. The unit is the 1.6-litre turbocharged V6 known as the Red Bull Ford DM01, built by Red Bull Powertrains in Milton Keynes, where Ben Hodgkinson leads the engine side while Wache handles the RB22 chassis.

According to RacingNews365 , the FIA's ADUO assessment revealed that Red Bull's internal combustion engine generated the highest output among all competitors on the grid. That makes a self-assessment of four or five rather intriguing. If this is the half-finished version, other teams likely have a reason to be nervous.

"You have to do more, and you also feel more responsible for what we can achieve," he said. He also sees the upside of owning the whole package: "Ultimately, we'll have more freedom. As you say, it's a success story. But you know, the journey isn't over yet. We have plenty of stuff to improve together."

Does the in-house building make life easier?

"So, I wouldn't say it's easier, because we have a lot more capacity and a lot more possibilities that we haven't explored and exploited yet.

"But the capacity and the potential to have a better performance are higher, and this is why we are doing this."

Engine people and chassis people don't think alike

Putting an engine department and a chassis department under one roof sounds like the most organised option, but Wache admits it wasn't as easy as it sounds. "The collaboration and the integration within the team are taking time because the way we work is a little bit different," he said, before adding: "Just by nature, the people on the engine and chassis side are quite different."

A big reason is the calendar. An engine takes far longer to develop than a chassis, so the two groups see problems and deadlines differently. "Anyway, it's a learning process for the full team because the lead time on a chassis is a lot quicker than an engine, so the way you see stuff is different, and the way we work with them is different compared to what we used to do when we were a customer."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

As a customer, Red Bull simply received a finished power unit and designed around it. Now the chassis team's tight turnarounds have to match an engine program that thinks in much longer cycles.

That is the real significance of the four-or-five rating. It suggests Red Bull is still building its own working processes as much as it is building horsepower, and that the performance it has shown so far comes before those habits have fully settled. A team admitting it is only about halfway through its first engine, while already becoming the benchmark, is either being very modest or very confident. With Red Bull, it's usually the second.

To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

articles.title: Brandon Woodruff shares injury update as Brewers push toward World Series
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers currently hold a 2-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. Milwaukee is in the driver’s seat,...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers currently hold a 2-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. Milwaukee is in the driver's seat , but there is still work to do as the best-of-seven NLCS shifts back to Dodger Stadium in LA. One pitcher who could give the Brewers a boost is Brandon Woodruff . It remains to be seen when he could return from his shoulder injury, but reports have suggested the Fall Classic remains in play for Woodruff — if Milwaukee reaches it, of course.

Woodruff threw a bullpen session and shared an injury update on Tuesday at Dodger Stadium, via Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.

"Brandon Woodruff threw a 31-pitch bullpen this afternoon at Dodger Stadium. The intent is being ramped up, and facing batters could be next. How's the stuff? 'If you ask me, it's pretty good,'" Hogg reported on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Woodruff would likely return in a bullpen role. He probably won't have enough time to build up as a starter. The fact that he threw 31 pitches on Tuesday is encouraging. If he can face batters without any issues, being activated for the World Series could be a possibility.

For now, Milwaukee is focused on the series against Los Angeles. The Brewers may hold a series lead, but they know what the Dodgers are capable of. This is an LA ball club that is not going to go away quietly.

Game 3 of the NLCS between the Brewers and Dodgers in Los Angeles is scheduled for 8 PM ET.

articles.title: Ex-Commanders WR Suddenly Cut by NFL Team Before Week 6
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders have been the story of Week 5 after the way their matchup with the New York Giants concluded.Ultimately, a late-game blunder by the...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have been the story of Week 5 after the way their matchup with the New York Giants concluded.

Ultimately, a late-game blunder by the Commanders led to a 27-27 tie.

Now sitting at 1-3-1, Washington shifts its focus to Week 6, when it takes on the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on "Monday Night Football."

Ahead of Week 6, the Commanders saw one of their former wide receivers hit the open market on Tuesday.

The Baltimore Ravens released 33-year-old journeyman wide receiver Chris Moore, who signed with the team on July 24.

Baltimore announced the move, writing, "We have released WR Chris Moore. We have also released WR Xavier Guillory from the Practice Squad."

Reports suggest Moore could re-sign with the Ravens ' practice squad as a vested veteran who doesn't have to clear waivers.

Moore's NFL Career and Time With Commanders

The Ravens drafted Moore in 2016, and he spent the first five years of his career in Baltimore before stints with the Houston Texans, Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals and Commanders in 2024 and 2025.

Moore didn't record any stats during his first season in Washington in 2024. However, he appeared in 14 games last season and started five, hauling in 11 receptions for 207 yards and one touchdown.

He has caught three passes for 63 yards and a touchdown this season with Baltimore. Across his career, Moore has recorded 152 receptions for 1,980 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Moore could give the Commanders another depth option at wide receiver, especially since he is familiar with Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn.

Washington has also dealt with injuries at the position through the first five weeks of the season.

However, no reports have indicated that Washington is pursuing any wide receivers on the open market.

articles.title: Four Goals Not Enough for Red Wings vs. Devils
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings’ experiment of moving Emmitt Finnie to center seems to be paying off but it won’t matter […]
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings' experiment of moving Emmitt Finnie to center seems to be paying off but it won't matter if the team can't play an effective overall game with more consistency.

Finnie's line, which includes rookie Michael Brandsegg-Nygard and Alex DeBrincat produced four goals. However, that wasn't enough as the Devils pulled out a 5-4 overtime win on a Jack Hughes game-winner.

DeBrincat scored twice, and Finnie and Brandsegg-Ngyard scored once for the Red Wings. Each of them was plus-4. DeBrincat's second goal tied the game 4-4 early in the third period.

Andrew Copp was minus-3 in the first 40 minutes of the game.

BRANDSEGG-NYGARD ABSOLUTELY ROOFS THIS SHOT ON THE 2 ON 1 OPPORTUNITY 🚀🚀🚀 pic.twitter.com/5LChr0bJ0E — PUCK'D Media (@PUCKD_) October 13, 2026

BRANDSEGG-NYGARD ABSOLUTELY ROOFS THIS SHOT ON THE 2 ON 1 OPPORTUNITY 🚀🚀🚀 pic.twitter.com/5LChr0bJ0E

The Red Wings went with 11 forwards and seven defensemen again in this game. Nate Danielson was the scratch up front. . . Defenseman Andreas Englund posted five hits for the Red Wings in the first two periods… Anton Johansson drew an assist on Finnie's goal for his first NHL point. . . . Brandsegg-Nygard posted six hits in the game.

The Devils erased a 2-1 Detroit lead with three second period goals (by former Red Wings player Anthony Mantha, plus Nico Hischier and Jesper Bratt.)

Detroit goalie John Gibson has given up 10 goals in his past two starts for the Red Wings.

The Red Wings are home again Thursday (7:30 p.m.) when they play the Philadelphia Flyers. Coach Rick Tocchet's Flyers team is 0-5-2 and has been outscored 28-8.

articles.title: Alex DeBrincat's 3 points not enough for Red Wings in OT loss to Devils
articles.summary: Alex DeBrincat had two goals and an assist for the Detroit Red Wings in a 5-4 overtime loss to the New Jersey Devils.
articles.body:
The second line answered for the Detroit Red Wings time and again, pushing back against an early onslaught.

Returning to Little Caesars Arena for another week, the Wings took on the New Jersey Devils in a battle of two of the top-shooting teams in the NHL. One of them backed that up from the start on on Tuesday, Oct. 13, and it wasn't the home team.

Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, both 21 years old, set up each other's goals, and veteran Alex DeBrincat, the left wing on the line, also had a multi-point night, but the Wings had to settle for one point when Jack Hughes scored in overtime to hand the Wings a 5-4 loss, dropping them to 1-3-2 on the season.

DeBrincat celebrated his second goal and third point of the night 5:46 into the third period when he one-timed a pass by Moritz Seider, tying the game.

See Detroit Red Wings return home for matchup with New Jersey Devils

Marco Kasper, J.T. Compher and Mason Appleton remained sidelined by injuries, and Nate Danielson was scratched from the lineup as the Wings went with 11 forwards and seven defensemen for the fourth time this season. Up front, Dylan Larkin was with Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond, Emmitt Finnie with Alex DeBrincat and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, Andrew Copp with Michael Rasmussen and Keegan Kolesar, and Sheldon Dries and Carter Mazur saw spot duty.

On the back end, Moritz Seider paired with Ben Chiarot, Justin Faulk with Albert Johansson, Anton Johansson with Andreas Englund and Axel Sandin-Pellikka also played.

The Wings couldn't get out of their zone the first several minutes and eventually it caught up to them with Stefan Noesen maneuvering a loose puck at his legs over to Evan Rodrigues for a 1-0 lead at 6:07, with shots at 3-0 at the time. Ex-Wing Anthony Mantha drew the second assist. It wasn't until the midpoint of the period that Jake Allen had to make a save, on Moritz Seider, and 12 minutes in, shots favored the Devils, 11-1.

Arvidsson looked like he would make something happen on a rush in the second half of the first period, driving the puck to the net through traffic but his shot went wide. Shots were 16-2 to the Devils when Finnie blasted out of the neutral zone and down the left flank, extending his stick to corral the puck Brandsegg-Nygard had sent into the zone, firing a shot that went in off the far post and made it 1-1 at 18:35. Anton Johansson earned his first career NHL point with the second assist. The Wings had three shots to New Jersey's 15 after 20 minutes.

The Wings came into the game averaging 32.8 shots per game, but only two goals. They made them count against the Devils, going up 2-1 on their fourth shot of the night. This time it was Finnie who found Brandsegg-Nygard with a pass across the slot, and Brandsegg-Nygard finishing the play when he ripped the puck from just inside the left circle for his second goal of the season.

The Wings grabbed momentum, only to give it back soon after. Dawson Mercer fired a pass across the ice and straight to Mantha, who was wide open with Justin Faulk trying to gap up and had time and space to make it 2-2 at 7:03 of the second period. Faulk was on the ice again during a penalty kill when Nico Hischier made short work of both him and Albert Johansson to be in position at the top of the crease to convert and make it 3-2, at 10:16.

DeBrincat became the third on the line to score, firing a shot from just inside the blue line and using Brandseg-Nygard as a screen, but again the momentum was short lived. A furious scramble by the net was saved when John Gibson pushed his right skate against the post, preventing anyone from poking it any further, only for Jesper Bratt to take advantage of a screened Gibson to make it 4-3 at 16:52, a minute and a half after DeBrincat's goals.

The Philadelphia Flyers on Thursday (7:30 p.m., ESPN+).

Contact Helene St. James at Hstjames@freepress.com. Read more on the Detroit Red Wings and sign up for our Red Wings newsletter .
authors: Helene St. James, Detroit Free Press

articles.title: Jack Hughes scores on a breakaway in OT, lifts Devils to a 5-4 win over Red Wings
articles.summary: DETROIT (AP) — Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the De...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday night.

New Jersey's Evan Rodrigues, Nico Hischier and Bratt scored tiebreaking goals and Anthony Mantha had a tying goal. Jake Allen stopped 22 shots for the Devils.

Alex DeBrincat had a pair of tying goals after Emmitt Finne and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scored to give the Red Wings a 2-1 lead.

Detroit's John Gibson made 32 saves, including a kick save that denied Arseny Gritsyuk on an odd-man rush late in regulation to send the game to overtime.

The Red Wings got off to a rough start, getting outshot 16-0 midway through the first period. New Jersey, though, didn't take full advantage as Rodrigues scored its only goal in the opening period.

Finne scored on Detroit's third shot with 1:25 left in the first period and Brandsegg-Nygard scored on the team's next shot early in the second period.

The Devils, hoping to get back to the playoffs after finishing seventh in the division last year, acquired Rodrigues in a trade and signed Mantha — a former Red Wing — in free agency to boost their third line.

Detroit, meanwhile, had a shaky offseason.

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded and the former captain is still on the team. Simon Edvinsson , a standout defenseman, remains unsigned as a restricted free agent.

Devils forward Luke Evangelista was out with an illness after feeling worse throughout the game Monday night against Ottawa and was replaced by Stefan Noesen. New Jersey defenseman Johnathan Kovacevic made his season debut after missing all of training camp recovering from knee surgery this past spring.

Devils: Host the New York Rangers on Thursday night.

Red Wings: Host Philadelphia on Thursday night.

articles.title: Michigan State OC Nick Sheridan previews matchup with Northwestern
articles.summary: Following their best outing of the season, MSU OC Nick Sheridan talked about his unit heading into a game with Northwestern.
articles.body:
Michigan State football may have lost their fourth consecutive game to Illinois this past week, but something clicked for the Spartans on offense in the contest. The Spartans scored a season high 37 points in the game, while getting 342 yards of total offense and scoring on 6-of-9 drives in the game.

It was a much needed performance from the offense, and it plays into the fact that Nick Sheridan has his unit developing week over week. Furthermore, the play calling from Sheridan was outstanding Saturday afternoon.

Now, it is time for the Spartans to turn the page to Northwestern, with MSU looking to replicate the success they had against Fighiting Illini to success against the Wildcats.

articles.title: Jury returns mixed verdict in Tyreek Hill civil battery case, awards $500,000 to ex-wife
articles.summary: Hill lost on two counts, won as to the rest.
articles.body:
The civil lawsuit brought by Tyreek Hill's ex-wife alleging multiple counts of battery and related legal claims has resulted in a verdict. Via Diana Moskovitz of Defector Media , the jury found Hill responsible for two counts of battery . He was found not responsible on the remaining counts.

The jury awarded Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury did not enter an award of punitive damages.

The jury's decision not to award punitive damages is curious. Battery is an intentional tort. In Florida, however, the law requires " clear and convincing evidence " of intentional misconduct. It's possible, in theory, that the jury found evidence of battery under the lower "preponderance of the evidence" standard but not "clear and convincing" proof, which is a higher bar.

The outcome becomes relevant to the NFL's ongoing Personal Conduct Policy review arising from the allegations Vaccaro initially made against Hill in a divorce filing. The findings represent a neutral determination that Hill more likely than not committed battery, twice. However, the Personal Conduct Policy does not automatically subject a player to discipline based solely on a civil verdict; the league will still need to perform its own investigation and reach a conclusion through the collectively-bargained process.

Regardless, the finding of two instances of civil battery, plus a $500,000 verdict, could cause one or more potentially interested teams to refrain from pursuing him. Especially since the league could still find that Hill violated the policy as to the two incidents on which Hill lost — and all incidents on which he prevailed.

articles.title: Rams OLB Myles Garrett won't return to practice this week
articles.summary: The Rams will have to wait at least another week to have Myles Garrett back at practice.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett is eligible to come off injured reserve at any time after missing the last four games, but he still needs more time to recover from knee surgery. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay confirmed on Tuesday that Garrett will not return to practice this week, meaning he will not come off IR just yet.

The Rams can open Garrett's 21-day practice window whenever they'd like, but if they do so, he will need to be activated off IR within those three weeks. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network said Tuesday that his understanding is it's a six-week recovery for Garrett, which would put him in line to return in Week 7.

McVay has not yet confirmed when Garrett will be back for Los Angeles, but the team will not rush him back – and understandably so. It's a long season, so the Rams want to make sure he's available down the stretch.

Garrett has played just one game this season, and even in that contest, he wasn't 100% healthy. He said as much after the Rams' season opener, admitting it was the worst version of himself that he could've put out there.

A few days after that loss to the 49ers, Garrett underwent knee surgery, which landed him on injured reserve.

In Garrett's place, the Rams have used Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart heavily, with Wesley Bailey and Desjuan Johnson backing them up. They've survived Garrett's absence, but they can't wait to get their prized offseason addition back in the lineup.

articles.title: Desert Ridge football controversy. Here's what we know
articles.summary: Desert Ridge High School football kicked the starting quarterback off the team last week. Then, 12 teammates were suspended.
articles.body:
Mesa Desert Ridge football coach Miles Smith kicked starting quarterback Gunner Brewer off the team last week. Then, 12 teammates supporting him were suspended .

According to the quarterback's mom, Brewer was dismissed from the team for changing a play given to him to run in a 14-12 win at Vail Cienega on Oct. 2. He was told by Smith, she said, on that Monday, Oct. 5, that he felt disrespected and that he was no longer part of the team.

Two days later, the team was brought together to discuss Brewer's dismissal. Offensive lineman Will Stark, according to his mom, stood up and asked who wanted to see their quarterback back. A large group raised their hand.

Shadow Ridge flag football team defeats Desert Ridge

Kristie Stark, Will's mom, said an assistant coach told them that if they didn't like their decision, they could leave. Twelve players left. They were subsequently suspended from the team. Their banners were removed and equipment taken out of their lockers, she said. Athletic director Kevin Swann, after meeting with players and coaches, sent a letter to the Desert Ridge parents, detailing his findings.

The players came to the Friday, Oct. 9, home game in a show of support. They tried to help with the inflatable Jaguar that the players run through before games, but were turned away, according to a parent. They sat in the stands, while Desert Ridge lost to Mesa Red Mountain, 49-7.

Kristie Stark and her son met with Swann and Smith on Monday, Oct. 12, at which time they were informed that Will would no longer be part of the team through the rest of the season. In a voice message left to a parent on Monday, Oct. 12, athletic director Kevin Swann said that the players, seven of whom were underclassmen, were suspended for the rest of the season but could return for winter workouts and for next season.

On Tuesday, Kristie Stark met with the principal, Scott Smith. She told The Republic in a text message, "Just had a GREAT conversation with the school principal. Very receptive." Stark couldn't immediately be reached after the text message.

The Jaguars (2-5) play host to Tempe Corona del Sol on Thursday, Oct. 15.

articles.title: High School Basketball: Nine area teams set to compete at 2027 Flyin’ To The Hoop
articles.summary: Springfield head coach Chris Wallace was excited to be in attendance. Getting to hear his team be announced Tuesday, Oct. 13, alongside other prominent state...
articles.body:
Springfield head coach Chris Wallace was excited to be in attendance.

Getting to hear his team be announced Tuesday, Oct. 13, alongside other prominent state and national basketball programs as a participant in the upcoming 24th annual Flyin' To The Hoop event at Trent Arena left the first-year head coach all smiles about the state of his team.

"We're not a flash in the pan team. We got some great freshman and great sophomores, and it's the sophomores that are going to really contribute," Wallace said. "We are going to be a tough out, and we're going to be exciting to watch. I think Springfield basketball is definitely back."

The Wildcats will be one of 30 teams playing at FTTH this season. It will be Springfield's first appearance since 2020.

Other Dayton-area teams selected to play are Alter, Bellbrook, Centerville, Chaminade Julienne, Fairmont, Northridge, Valley View and Wayne.

The four-day event will be held as typical during Martin Luther King Holiday weekend from Jan. 15-18, 2027.

Bellbrook, Centerville, Fairmont are matched with some of the top teams coming in from out of state. Alter and CJ will play a Greater Catholic League Co-Ed game against one another. Northridge, Valley View and Wayne get to test themselves against other outstanding teams from Ohio.

As of Tuesday's announcement, there are six 5-star prospects and 29 others rated as 4-stars that will appear at FTTH. Asa Montgomery, a 5-star committed to Duke that plays at Hillgrove (Ga.), is ranked eighth overall in the 247Sports composite rankings for the class of 2027 and is the highest-rated recruit in the country set to appear.

Other notable recruits set to play are Pickerington Central's Landon Evans, a 3-star who committed to Wright State in July, and Xavier-commit Brandon Mason Jr., a 4-star who plays at Link Academy (Mo.)

The schedule will follow similar trends as used in recent years.

The Friday night slate has several national teams featuring multiple top prospects. Local teams begin Saturday and are interspersed with matchups against Ohio and other national teams. The event concludes Monday with host Fairmont's game and a small school showcase.

"We're going to have 11 of the top-20 Ohio teams regardless of their division," FTTH president Eric Horstman said. "We're going to have some of the top national teams. There's some stories behind some of them, there is a reason why you see these. You might not recognize the name right away, but there's a reason why they're coming to this event."

Centerville will be making its 21st appearance at FTTH. The Elks have participated more than any other school. Wayne is next on the list and is back on the schedule for the 20th consecutive event.

"When we show up, everything is first class. The way you're treated, the way the players are treated, how organized everything is, everything stays on time," Wayne head coach Nathan Martindale said. "We truly believe this is the number one showcase event in the country."

The 2027 event will be the first time Flyin' To The Hoop utilizes a shot clock for all contests. The move was approved by the Ohio High School Basketball Coaches Association in August and joins a list of 19 events in Ohio allowed to have a shot clock.

Two teams from the Nike EYBL Scholastic League will be playing: CIA Bella Vista out of Arizona, and Link Academy from Missouri. Both will play two games, including one against one another on Saturday.

Flyin' To The Hoop entered into a partnership with the national prep league beginning with last year's event.

articles.title: 👀Two-time champion dreams of Atlético Nacional return to coach youngsters
articles.summary: Former midfielder and two-time title winner with Atlético Nacional, Jairo "el Viejo" Patiño, has openly expressed his desire to return to the club, this time...
articles.body:
Former midfielder and two-time title winner with Atlético Nacional, Jairo "el Viejo" Patiño, has openly expressed his desire to return to the club, this time as part of the youth academy's coaching staff.

Speaking to El Colombiano, the Cali-born coach revealed that he has had very positive talks with the club's management: "I'm fully available now; we've already held meetings, and my dream is to be part of the club's youth development program." Patiño has experience managing clubs such as Llaneros, Cúcuta Deportivo, Bogotá FC, and Real Cartagena.

A winning legacy in Colombian professional football

During his playing career, Patiño won the 2011 Apertura tournament and the 2011 Copa Colombia with the Medellín-based club. He also earned 37 caps for Colombia and had notable spells at River Plate, Newell's, and Banfield.

articles.title: 'Never say no to Big Woo': Could Brandon Woodruff pitch in a World Series?
articles.summary: With the Brewers two wins away from the World Series, Brandon Woodruff threw a high-intent bullpen at Dodger Stadium
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – As Brandon Woodruff brought his glove set in front of his face and gripped the ball with his right hand in the bullpen beyond the right-field fence at Dodger Stadium, there was far more intent in his eyes than the standard off-day bullpen that he's thrown hundreds of times in his career.

For 31 pitches as the Milwaukee Brewers worked out on an off-day Oct. 13, Woodruff stared down the mitt, oftentimes muttering bits of self-talk into the glove.

"For me, I'm not really holding back," said the right-hander. "I'm going as hard as my body will let me right now. It's just where we're at with everything."

That Woodruff and the Brewers are even here – weighing the 33-year-old as an option for a potential World Series roster – to begin with feels somewhat like a far-fetched reality.

Less than two months ago, the public expectation was Woodruff would be undergoing a second shoulder surgery, a procedure that put him ever pitching in the major leagues again in question. Woodruff revealed in late August he, it turned out out, didn't need surgery. And not only that, he and the Brewers weren't ruling out a return in the postseason.

With Milwaukee ahead two games to none as the National League Championship Series shifts to Los Angeles for three games, Woodruff threw his first high-intent bullpen since resuming a throwing program in early September (he threw a light touch-and-feel off the mound two days prior).

"What I set out to do was to be able to have a shot to do it," Woodruff said. "It's one of those things that it's hard to process that can happen.

"If it does happen, the competitive juices take over and I'm not worried about this [being] my first time pitching in a major-league game in three months. I'm not looking at that. I'm looking at today.

"We'll just see what happens, but if I have the opportunity I'll be ready to go."

The next step for Woodruff is to face live hitters, which could happen as soon as this weekend if he recovers well from his bullpen. That phase will be critical for the Brewers as they weigh the decision of placing him on a possible World Series roster – and all the implications that come with that.

"We'll have to see live BPs and stuff like that," said pitching coach Jim Henderson. "Just make sure he's progressing. The biggest thing is his health and his future. And if it happens to line up with him pitching this season, then great.

"I think we have to be aware of where the team's at, be aware of where he's at. If it works, it works. We're not going to force it or put pressure on it. But if it does, he's also performed really really well when he's on the mound.

"So it's never a question of whether we want him out there. We do. It's a matter of lining it up."

What, realistically, would the Brewers need to see from Woodruff to go from not pitching since July 4 to using a World Series roster spot on him?

"It's probably going to be based on his health and strength and velo," Henderson said. "That's going to be a big determining factor."

Woodruff's velocity in the bullpen session wasn't zipping in the mid-90s, but the Brewers also don't necessarily need it to be where it was when Woodruff was healthy this year.

Their brass has seen him throw in the upper-80s in side sessions and rehab assignments only to ramp it up in-game each of the last two years. Whether he has the ability to do that this time and coming off of this injury is something Henderson, pitching coach Chris Hook, manager Pat Murphy and the front office will have to decide, but having seen it happen before seems to bring about confidence given the adrenaline that would come with a Fall Classic stage.

And speaking of confidence, the Brewers have plenty of that in Woodruff's execution – so much so that a World Series comeback is entirely possible largely because of that trust.

"I think his execution's going to be there," Henderson said. "He's always been a high executor, even when he was going through the stuff earlier this year. I don't think execution's going to be a problem."

Still, Woodruff's stuff would almost certainly need to reach a certain threshold for this to actually take place. So, where is Woodruff's stuff at right now?

"If you ask me, it's pretty good," he said.

The plot, as Murphy likes to say, thickens. Considering the Brewers haven't used three pitchers in their bullpen at all through six postseason games – a point to which Murphy said before the workout that "this isn't tryouts – it's not as if there's no way to make room for him on the roster.

"It's a nice little piece to this," Henderson said. "You'll never say no to 'Big Woo' out there."

articles.title: Penn State football linebacker Alex Tatsch to miss rest of the season
articles.summary: As Penn State football prepares for a big road test against Michigan, the Nittany Lions just lost another promising young defender.
articles.body:
Penn State football 's injury situation just got a lot worse as sophomore linebacker Alex Tatsch will miss the rest of the season due to injury. The news was first reported on Penn State football play-by-play announcer Steve Jones' radio show.

Tatsch missed the USC game due to an injury that was sustained in practice. The Latrobe, Pa. native appeared in four games this season, recording 11 total tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a sack and a forced fumble.

Head coach Matt Campbell was high on Tatsch when he arrived in Happy Valley, but now the promising defender's 2026 season is cut short.

The Nittany Lions already had injury problems before losing Tatsch, with redshirt sophomore Max Granville out for the season . Not to mention star wide receiver Koby Howard has yet to return from his injury, although Campbell and the staff are expecting Howard to return this season.

More defensive help may be on the way as well, as defensive end LaVar Arrington II and linebacker Cam Smith are both expected to return before October concludes. Still, losing Tatsch is a significant blow to a team that has several issues and could use all the help it can get before traveling to Ann Arbor and facing Michigan in the Big House.
